# firecrawl download (invoked as `firecrawl x download`)

> **Experimental.** `download` is available under the `firecrawl x` command group.

**Prerequisite:** `download` requires authentication (no keyless free tier); without credentials the CLI prompts an interactive login.

Maps the site origin first to discover pages, then scrapes each one into nested directories under `.firecrawl/`. Use `--include-paths` to scope a non-root URL to one section. Automated runs always pass `-y` — without it the command opens an interactive wizard that blocks on a prompt.

## Quick start

```bash
# With screenshots
firecrawl x download https://docs.example.com --screenshot --limit 20 -y

# Multiple formats (each saved as its own file per page)
firecrawl x download https://docs.example.com --format markdown,links --screenshot --limit 20 -y
# Creates per page: index.md + links.txt + screenshot.png

# Filter to specific sections
firecrawl x download https://docs.example.com --include-paths "/features,/sdks" -y

# Skip translations
firecrawl x download https://docs.example.com --exclude-paths "/zh,/ja,/fr,/es,/pt-BR" -y
```

Run `firecrawl x download --help` for the full option list, including which scrape options download supports.

For "the first N pages" or named pages, `map` the section first, pick those URLs in the site's own order, and pass them with `--include-paths`: `--limit` alone takes whichever pages it finds first.

**Done when:** the command exits successfully and the files you meant to save exist under `.firecrawl/` (list them).

## See also

- [firecrawl-map](../firecrawl-map/SKILL.md) — just discover URLs without downloading
- [firecrawl-scrape](../firecrawl-scrape/SKILL.md) — scrape individual pages
- [firecrawl-crawl](../firecrawl-crawl/SKILL.md) — bulk extract as JSON (not local files)
- [firecrawl-build-scrape](https://github.com/firecrawl/skills/tree/main/skills/build/firecrawl-build-scrape) — building bulk extraction into an app instead of running it here

I pulled every page under `docs.slack.dev/reference/methods` (338 unique methods) and read the "Rate Limits" line from each one. Eleven extra pages were `.md` duplicates of real methods, so I used the tier on the real page. One of them (`chat.postEphemeral`) had no non-`.md` copy, so its tier comes from the `.md` page.

## Tier 1 (1+ per minute): 17 methods
- `admin.apps.uninstall`
- `admin.conversations.restrictAccess.removeGroup`
- `admin.teams.create`
- `admin.usergroups.addChannels`
- `admin.usergroups.create`
- `admin.usergroups.fetch`
- `admin.usergroups.update`
- `admin.users.unsupportedVersions.export`
- `apps.icon.set`
- `apps.manifest.create`
- `apps.manifest.delete`
- `apps.manifest.update`
- `apps.uninstall`
- `conversations.listConnectInvites`
- `rtm.connect`
- `rtm.start` (deprecated)
- `team.externalTeams.disconnect`

## "Special rate limits apply": 19 methods
- `admin.analytics.messages.metadata`
- `agents.conversations.archive`
- `agents.conversations.create`
- `agents.conversations.listViews`
- `agents.conversations.removeView`
- `agents.conversations.setCommands`
- `agents.conversations.setProperties`
- `agents.conversations.setView`
- `apps.event.authorizations.list`
- `assistant.search.context`
- `assistant.threads.setStatus`
- `auth.test`
- `blocks.validate`
- `chat.getPermalink`
- `chat.postMessage`
- `oauth.v2.access`
- `oauth.v2.user.access`
- `tooling.tokens.rotate`

That is 18 above plus `chat.getPermalink`'s `.md` copy, which is the same method. The real count is 18 methods.

The page for `chat.postMessage` says "special", but Slack's rate-limit docs describe it as roughly 1 message per second per channel with short bursts allowed. If your rate limits come from posting, that is the one to look at.

## conversations.* methods (31)

| Tier | Methods |
|---|---|
| **Tier 1** | `listConnectInvites` |
| **Tier 2** | `acceptSharedInvite`, `archive`, `canvases.create`, `close`, `create`, `externalInvitePermissions.set`, `inviteShared`, `list`, `rename`, `requestSharedInvite.approve`, `requestSharedInvite.deny`, `requestSharedInvite.list`, `setPurpose`, `setTopic`, `unarchive` |
| **Tier 3** | `approveSharedInvite`, `declineSharedInvite`, `history`, `info`, `invite`, `join`, `kick`, `leave`, `mark`, `open`, `replies` |
| **Tier 4** | `members` |

No `conversations.*` method has a special tier.

The two that commonly cause trouble are `conversations.list` at Tier 2 (about 20 per minute) and `conversations.history` and `conversations.replies` at Tier 3 (about 50 per minute). Caching channel lists and paginating with a larger `limit` are the usual fixes.

## Deprecated, as stated on the method's own page
- **`rtm.start`**: it has a "Deprecated" badge, and its description says to use `rtm.connect` instead.
- **`files.upload`**: the page says it has been deprecated and was to be sunset on November 12, 2025. The replacement is `files.getUploadURLExternal` plus `files.completeUploadExternal`.
- **`users.setActive`**: its description reads "Deprecated and non-functional."

Some other pages mention deprecation only for a single argument or behaviour, not the whole method:
- `reactions.add`: the `file` and `file_comment` arguments.
- `agents.conversations.setProperties`: the `status` and `title` arguments.
- `agents.conversations.setView`: the `label` argument.
- `users.list`: retrieving presence.
- `chat.postMessage`: passing a username as `channel`.

Nearly every page lists `deprecated_endpoint` and `method_deprecated` among its error codes. That is boilerplate, so I ignored it.

## Caveats
- I classified methods by the rate-limit line on each page. I did not check each page's other sections for notes such as "this method behaves as Tier X for large workspaces".
- Tier 1 has no per-app or per-workspace headroom. A few calls a minute will trigger a 429, so check whether any of these are in a loop. The usual suspects are the `admin.usergroups.*` and `apps.manifest.*` methods.
- The pages are in `/tmp/fcdiag-c1-z08qtqsi/slackdocs/.firecrawl/`. The tier table I built is at `/tmp/fcdiag-c1-z08qtqsi/tiers.txt`. The `.md` duplicates appear in that table with a `NONE` tier, so ignore those rows.

If you tell me which methods your app calls most, I can narrow this to those.
